- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 2–4% per day.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint of sentiment transition, not end of period.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67); use 15-day rolling average of sentiment to smooth and adjust forecast mean.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overconfident; apply downward bias proportional to sentiment volatility (e.g., 0.5x sentiment variance).
